findings.evidence: mathlib mem_iff_lt_rowLen: `(i,j) ∈ μ ↔ j < μ.rowLen i`; armLength = μ.rowLen c.1 - c.2 - 1 (line 141).
findings.fix: Drop `(h : c ∈ μ)`; prove by `rw [mem_iff_lt_rowLen]; simp only [armLength]; omega`. This also refutes the docstring claim (lines ~23-25) that such lemmas would be false for the junk value.
findings.issue: `armLength_eq_zero_iff (h : c ∈ μ)`: `h` is unused. `armLength μ c = 0` is `μ.rowLen c.1 - c.2 - 1 = 0`, i.e. `μ.rowLen c.1 ≤ c.2 + 1`, which is definitionally `(c.1, c.2+1) ∉ μ` via `mem_iff_lt_rowLen`; the iff holds for every `c`. `omega` proves it without `h`.

findings.evidence: mem_iff_lt_colLen: `(i,j) ∈ μ ↔ i < μ.colLen j`; legLength = μ.colLen c.2 - c.1 - 1 (line 146).
findings.fix: Drop `(h : c ∈ μ)`; `rw [mem_iff_lt_colLen]; simp only [legLength]; omega`.
findings.issue: `legLength_eq_zero_iff (h : c ∈ μ)`: same unused hypothesis. `μ.colLen c.2 - c.1 - 1 = 0` ↔ `μ.colLen c.2 ≤ c.1 + 1` ↔ `(c.1+1, c.2) ∉ μ`, independent of `h`.

findings.evidence: For c ∉ μ: armLength = legLength = 0 so LHS holds, and (c.1,c.2+1),(c.1+1,c.2) ∉ μ so RHS holds.
findings.fix: Once the two zero-iff lemmas lose `h`, drop it here too: `rw [← armLength_eq_zero_iff, ← legLength_eq_zero_iff, hookLength]; omega`.
findings.issue: `hookLength_eq_one_iff (h : c ∈ μ)`: `h` only forwards to the two lemmas above and is otherwise unnecessary — for `c ∉ μ` both sides are true (hookLength = 1, both neighbours absent), so the iff holds unconditionally.

summary: The arm/leg zero-length lemmas (and the derived corner criterion) carry a `c ∈ μ` hypothesis that is provably unused; the statements hold for all cells. Otherwise the material sits at the natural level, with the single-column formula correctly derived from the single-row case by transposition rather than duplicated.
